w: The boat from [WP] leaves at [WT]. Take the [WB] to the ticket desk before you board.
Meet me at [WL] at [WT]. I’ll be the one wearing the [WW].
Please leave the [WO] on the counter at [WL]. [WN] will collect it.
I moved the picnic to [WP]. Bring [WF] and tell [WN] the new location.
I put the spare [WO] in the [WB]. It’s waiting at [WL].
We start our walk at [WP] and stop for [WF]. Our guide is [WN].
A bus is picking us up at [WL] at [WT]. Pack your [WW] in case it gets cold.
For tomorrow’s display, put the [WO] beside the [WC] sign at [WL].
Our first stop is [WP]. Stay for [WD], then meet [WN] back at the van.
I left [WF] in the kitchen two doors down from [WL]. The note is for [WN].
The staff at [WL] found my [WW]. Their lost-property desk opens at [WT].
Send [WN] to [WP] with the [WB]. I’ve already packed what we need.
A [WA] wandered into the garden at [WL]. [WN] showed it back outside.
I’m saving [WF] for our break at [WT]. There’s room for us outside [WL].
Leave your [WB] under the table at [WL]. A [WC] ribbon marks our seats.
We’ll be painting [WX] at [WP]. Bring a spare brush for [WN].
[WN] borrowed the [WO] at [WT]. Ask when they’ll be able to return it.
I pinned the sketch of [WX] near the [WC] poster at [WL].
The shortest trail starts at [WP]. Expect [WD] on foot and pack the [WB].
I picked up [WF] for [WN]. Leave it wrapped until [WT].
At [WT], meet [WN] outside [WL]. They’re handling the check-in.
The box labelled [WC] contains my [WO]. It’s still at [WL].
The guide spotted a [WA] at [WP]. We arrived about [WD] later.
[WN] needs the [WB] as soon as [WL] opens.
There’s a drawing of [WX] on the [WC] card. Show it to [WN].
I bought [WF] during a stop at [WP]. Save half for [WN].
The driver waited [WD] at [WP]. The message for [WN] is on the dashboard.
Look for the [WC] marker at [WP]. That’s where I dropped my [WW].
The last table near [WL] is ours until [WT]. Place the [WB] underneath it.
I put a photo of [WX] in the [WB]. Deliver it to [WN].
A [WA] crossed the footpath at [WP]. We stayed still for [WD] to watch.
When [WN] gets to [WL], give them the [WO] from the drawer.
Meet our driver at [WP] at [WT]. Put any loose items in the [WB].
There’s a [WC] tag on my [WW]. Please take it to [WL].
[WN] is planning a break at [WP]. I volunteered to bring [WF].
We heard the clock strike at [WT] while we were near [WL]. [WN] checked the time.
The new mural at [WL] shows [WX]. The artist painted a [WC] border around it.
I spent [WD] looking for the [WO]. It was in the [WB] all along.
At [WP], we unpacked [WF] and spotted a [WA] across the path.
[WN] ordered prints of [WX]. We can collect them at [WL].
Before heading to [WP], collect the [WW] that [WN] left with me.
The guide wore a [WC] badge at [WP]. I spoke with them for [WD].
We’re meeting at [WL] once [WN] has picked up the [WB].
Set out [WF] at [WT]. Keep a place free at the table for [WN].
The [WO] belongs in the [WB]. Both will be picked up from [WL].
I took a picture of a [WA] near [WP]. [WN] wants a copy.
There’s a drawing of [WX] in the [WC] folder. Leave it at [WL].
We waited [WD] at [WL] while someone went back for the [WB].
[WN] hung their [WW] by the doorway at [WL].
We had room for [WF] after our walk through [WP]. We stopped for [WD].
Follow the [WC] arrows to [WP]. Hand the map to [WN] when you arrive.
I found the [WO] at [WL]. The label on it says [WN].
The morning group meets at [WP] at [WT]. We’ll spend [WD] there.
The packet contains a sketch of [WX] for [WN]. Leave it in the [WB].
I ate [WF] outside [WL]. I left my [WW] on the bench.
A [WA] sat near the [WC] marker at [WP]. We gave it plenty of room.
Our porter moved the [WB] to [WL]. Tell [WN] where it is.
My reservation at [WL] is for [WT]. If I’m late, ask for [WN].
I’d like the [WC] print of [WX]. Put it in the [WB] if it fits.
Please return the [WO] at [WT]. I’ll be waiting outside [WL].
[WN] came to [WP] with [WF]. We shared it before taking the path back.
The [WA] stayed near our group for [WD]. We were visiting [WP].
I left the [WW] beside the [WB] at [WL]. Take both with you.
There’s a [WC] notice at [WL]. It says [WN] moved the meeting.
I promised [WN] a print of [WX]. We’re collecting it at [WT].
We’re taking the slower route from [WP]. Allow [WD] and bring [WF].
The [WO] is upstairs at [WL]. I need it by [WT].
Follow [WN] to [WP]. You can spot them by their [WW].
I signed the [WC] card and put it in the [WB] for [WN].
Someone took a photo of [WX] while we were at [WP]. We saw it at [WT].
Bring [WF] to [WL] if you get there before [WT].
We watched a [WA] from a bench at [WP]. [WN] knew what it was.
The [WB] and the [WO] arrived at [WL]. Please check that both are yours.
The [WC] door at [WL] will be unlocked at [WT].
[WN] can spare [WD] to show us around [WP]. Ask before we set off.
I folded the map of [WP] around a drawing of [WX]. It’s in the [WB].
Keep [WF] for tomorrow’s visitor, [WN]. Leave it on the counter at [WL].
I wore the [WW] at [WP] yesterday. I took it off at [WT].
At [WT] I’ll bring the [WO] to [WL] and wait by the door.
A [WA] came right up to a [WC] sign near [WP]. It turned around after a moment.
I stuck a picture of [WX] on the wall at [WL]. [WN] picked the frame.
The ride to [WP] takes [WD]. I put our tickets in the [WB].
[WN] found a [WO] when we stopped at [WP]. It was beside the path.
The [WW] with a [WC] label is for [WN]. I have a spare at home.
I’ll buy [WF] on the way to [WL]. See you at [WT].
The notice at [WP] says to wait [WD]. Our contact there is [WN].
The courier will arrive at [WL] at [WT]. Hand them the [WB] with our return label.
[WN] saw a [WA] outside [WL]. It was gone before I came out.
I packed the [WO] and a postcard of [WX]. Look in the [WB].
Our group photo at [WP] took [WD] to arrange. [WN] was holding the camera.
I’m picking up [WF] at [WT]. I’ll share it with [WN] on the way home.
The [WC] slip at [WL] lists the next session at [WT].
We stopped at [WP] because I needed to fix my [WW]. It took [WD].
[WN] is writing about [WX]. We’ll meet at [WL] to look over the draft.
Please set aside the [WO] with the [WC] label. I’ll pick it up at [WT].
At [WL] I traded our spare print of [WX] for [WF]. Everyone got a share.
The [WB] was a gift from [WN]. I opened it during our trip to [WP].
I waited [WD] for my train before I realised I’d left my [WW] at [WL].
Head to [WP] at [WT]. Sit near the [WC] marker until the group arrives.
s: At [SE], you ate [SF] before [SN] could serve it. Give your apology.
You thanked [SN] for organising [SE] while holding [SO]. You’d thanked the wrong person. Apologise.
You left [SB] on the only seat reserved for [SN] at [SL]. Apologise.
You announced [SE] was at [ST]. [SN] had given you the correct time twice. Apologise.
You posted the surprise details [SD] early in the chat for [SE], where [SN] could see them. Apologise.
You put a [SC] sign outside [SL] and sent everyone the wrong way for [SD]. Apologise.
You told [SN] there was enough [SF] for everyone at [SE]. There was just one serving. Apologise.
You arrived at [SL] dressed as [SR] because you thought [SE] had a costume theme. Apologise for interrupting.
You dropped [SO] onto [SB] just as [SN] started the demonstration. Apologise.
You renamed the group chat for [SE] to “[SH]” and forgot [SN] was presenting from it. Apologise.
You brought [SF] to [SL] and quietly ate it while [SN] went to find plates. Apologise.
You blamed a [SA] for the noise at [SL]. [SN] had a video proving it was you. Come clean.
In [SE]’s photo, you held up a [SC] card that completely hid [SN]. Apologise.
You left [SO] behind at [SL] and made everyone wait [SD] while you looked for it. Apologise.
You put a note about [SF] in [SB] and told [SN] it held the evening’s schedule. Apologise.
At [ST], you sent “[SH]” to the chat for [SE]. It was supposed to go to one friend. Apologise.
You needed one volunteer at [SE]. You pointed at [SN] and handed them [SO] before asking. Apologise.
You turned up at [SL] with [SB] full of [SF]. The room had been booked for a quiet meeting. Apologise.
You did an impression of [SR] for [SD] after [SN] asked you to stop. Apologise.
You promised to watch [SO] at [SL]. You went looking for [SF] and forgot. Apologise.
You used [SB] that belonged to [SN] as a prop at [SE] without asking. Apologise.
You said you’d reserve [SL] at [ST]. [SN] got there and found no booking. Apologise.
You stuck a [SC] label on [SO]. The label made [SN] take it to the wrong room. Apologise.
You said there was a [SA] outside [SL], so everyone left [SE] to look. You’d misread a poster. Apologise.
You meant to bring [SF] for [SN] at [SE]. You brought an empty plate. Apologise.
You pulled the [SC] curtain at [SL] [SD] too early. Apologise to the people backstage.
You sent [SN] a message saying “[SH]” at [ST]. It was their first message from you. Apologise.
You dropped [SO] while playing [SR] at [SE], then pretended it was part of the act. Apologise.
You spent [SD] describing [SF] to [SN] during their quiet break. Apologise.
You changed the route to [SL] at [ST] but told only [SN]. Apologise to everyone who missed the update.
You put a [SC] ribbon on [SB] and sent it home with [SN]. It belonged to someone else. Apologise.
You started telling a story about a [SA] just as [SN] was making a toast at [SE]. Apologise.
You hid [SO] at [SL] so you could make a grand entrance with it. Everyone waited [SD]. Apologise.
You asked [SN] to save [SF] for later, then gave their portion away at [SE]. Apologise.
You recorded your rehearsal as [SR] at [SL] and accidentally sent it to [SN]. Apologise.
A note saying “[SH]” fell out of [SB] in front of [SN]. Explain and apologise.
You put [SO] on the only clear table at [SL] for [SD] while everyone tried to set up. Apologise.
You thought [SE] had finished at [ST], so you began stacking chairs while [SN] was still speaking. Apologise.
You gave a prize meant for [SN] to the person carrying [SB] at [SE]. Apologise.
You replaced a slide at [SE] with a picture of a [SA] and coloured it [SC]. Apologise for the interruption.
At [SL], you let [SN] queue [SD] for a table you’d already given away. Apologise.
You asked [SN] to bring [SF] to [SE] and failed to tell them you’d already ordered it. Apologise.
You tried to lead everyone to [SL] using a [SC] arrow you drew at [ST]. It pointed backwards. Apologise.
You got an early look at [SO] in [SB] and told [SN] before the reveal. Apologise.
You called yourself [SR] on the sign-in sheet at [SE] and made extra work for [SN]. Apologise.
You parked [SB] against the door at [SL]. It took [SN] several tries to get in. Apologise.
You said a [SA] had knocked over [SO]. [SN] saw you knock it over yourself. Apologise.
You promised to call [SN] about [SE] at [ST]. Instead, you sent a blank message and went out. Apologise.
You used [SF] as a centrepiece for [SE], then told [SN] it wasn’t for eating. Apologise.
You handed [SN] a [SC] envelope at [ST]. It contained your shopping list. Apologise.
Your [SR] sketch ran [SD] over time at [SE]. Apologise to the next performer.
You sent [SN] to retrieve [SO] from [SL]. You had it with you. Apologise.
You announced that [SF] was cancelled at [SE] because you’d mixed up two notes from [SN]. Apologise.
You greeted a [SA] much more warmly than you greeted [SN] when you arrived at [SL]. Apologise playfully.
You mistook the [SC] sign for the exit before [SE] had even started. [SN] followed you. Apologise.
You put a “[SH]” label on [SB] just before [SN] gave a tour. Apologise for the awkward moment.
You said it would take [SD] to set up [SO] at [SL]. You hadn’t opened the instructions. Apologise.
You said [SN] could park near [SL] at [ST], forgetting the entrance was closed. Apologise.
You took [SF] from the table at [SE] because you thought [SN] had put it aside for you. Apologise.
You dressed as [SR] to make [SN] laugh, then forgot to remove the costume before [SE] started. Apologise.
You moved [SO] from [SL] to tidy up, then left [SN] without it. Apologise.
You left [SB] in the middle of the photo at [SE]. It hid the [SC] sign everyone came to see. Apologise.
You told [SN] that [SF] would arrive at [ST]. You hadn’t actually placed the order. Apologise.
You repeated a story about a [SA] to [SN] for [SD] before realising they’d told it to you. Apologise.
You added “[SH]” to the shared notes for [SE] while [SN] was reading them aloud. Apologise.
You returned [SO] at [ST] to [SL] on the wrong day. Apologise for the mix-up.
You kept [SN] waiting at [SL] for [SD] because you went to the other entrance. Apologise.
You left [SF] in [SB] and forgot to mention it until after [SE]. Apologise.
Your [SC] decoration blew across [SL] just as [SN] opened the doors. Apologise and offer to help.
You described [SR] as the evening’s special guest at [SE] without telling [SN] it was a joke. Apologise.
You placed [SO] on [SB] and forgot to tell [SN] where to find it. Apologise.
You called seat numbers at [SE] using [SN]’s list. You skipped an entire row at [ST]. Apologise.
You photographed a [SA] at [SL] instead of saving a seat for [SN]. Apologise.
You served [SF] on a [SC] display plate that [SN] was setting aside. Apologise.
You put a recording titled “[SH]” on the playlist at [SE]. [SN] had to stop it mid-introduction. Apologise.
You kept talking as [SR] at [SL] for [SD]. The person you were meant to greet walked past. Apologise.
You asked everyone to bring [SB] to [SE] when [SN] only needed one. Apologise.
You thought [SO] was a giveaway at [SL]. [SN] told you afterward it belonged to the venue. Apologise.
You promised to pick up [SF] at [ST]. [SN] had to leave dinner to get it instead. Apologise.
You raised a [SC] card at [SE] to ask one question. [SN] thought you wanted to take over. Apologise for causing confusion.
A [SA] appeared outside [SL]. You interrupted [SN]’s story to describe it. Apologise.
You spent [SD] showing [SN] how to pack [SB] after they’d already packed it. Apologise.
You asked a friend dressed as [SR] to announce [SE] at [ST]. It was supposed to be a surprise. Apologise.
You texted “[SH]” to [SN] instead of directions to [SL]. Apologise.
You took [SO] off the table before [SE] ended. [SN] still needed it. Apologise.
You brought the [SC] decorations to [SL] [SD] after the decorations team had finished. Apologise.
You arranged [SF] on the wrong table at [SE]. [SN] had to move it during their break. Apologise.
You announced a [SA] sighting at [ST] at [SL]. You had seen it the previous day. Apologise.
You asked [SN] to hold [SB] for [SD] and forgot to come back. Apologise.
You meant to dress as [SR] for [SE], but you wore the costume to [SL] a day early. Apologise for the confusion.
You wrote “[SH]” on a [SC] card and left it in front of [SN] during their presentation. Apologise.
You borrowed [SO] to fix something at [SL]. [SN] waited for it while you forgot to return it. Apologise.
You refused to cut [SF] until [ST], even after [SN] said the guests had to leave. Apologise.
You treated a [SA] as the unofficial mascot of [SE] and interrupted [SN]’s welcome to announce it. Apologise.
You chalked a [SC] marker on the ground near [SL]. It sent the next group on a [SD] detour. Apologise.
You told [SN] to bring [SB] at [ST], then texted them from the wrong meeting point. Apologise.
You practised an entrance as [SR] at [SE] without checking whether [SN] was still on stage. Apologise.
You presented [SO] as the grand prize at [SE]. [SN] had only lent it to you. Apologise.
You grabbed [SF] for your walk to [SL] and forgot [SN] ordered it for later. Apologise.
At [ST], a message saying “[SH]” went to [SN] alone, even though it concerned the whole group. Apologise.
You borrowed the [SC] marker at [SL] and misplaced it inside [SB]. Apologise.
You spent [SD] trying to get a photo of a [SA] during [SE], leaving your group short-handed. Apologise.
You moved [SO] that [SN] needed during [SE], then couldn’t remember which table it was on. Apologise.
You delayed [SE] by [SD] waiting for someone you thought was dressed as [SR]. Apologise.
You delivered [SF] at [ST] to [SL] but never told the people expecting it. Apologise.
You wrote “[SH]” on the board at [SL] before [SN] arrived to use it. Apologise.
You saw [SN] carry [SB] into [SL] and assumed they were the person assigned to clear the room. Apologise.
You asked everyone at [SE] to follow a [SC] marker at [ST], then realised there were two. Apologise.
You blamed a [SA] for why you arrived [SD] late to [SE]. Apologise to the people who waited.
You misplaced [SO] in [SB] while helping [SN] and spent the next hour blaming the room layout. Apologise.
You volunteered [SN] to introduce [SR] at [SE]. They heard about it from the audience. Apologise.
You put [SF] away at [ST] because you thought [SE] was over. Apologise to anyone who missed out.
You handed out [SC] slips at [SL] and used one to tell [SN] the wrong seat number. Apologise.
You told [SN] to wait [SD] at [SL] before reading the rest of the message yourself. Apologise.
You used “[SH]” as a group password for [SE] and announced it aloud to everyone at [SL]. Apologise for the commotion.
You carried [SO] to [SL] in [SB] and walked out with both just before the handover. Apologise.
You imitated [SR] while explaining a simple task to [SN]. It took [SD]. Apologise.
You put a picture of a [SA] on a [SC] sign at [SE] and people mistook it for an instruction. Apologise.
You said [SF] tasted like cardboard in front of [SN] at [SE]. They’d made it. Apologise.
You booked [SL] for [ST] and gave [SN] the date from a different booking. Apologise.
You set down [SB] where [SN] had put [SO]. It took them a while to find their thing. Apologise.
You used “[SH]” as the title for [SN]’s presentation at [SE]. They found out on stage. Apologise.
You let [SN] go looking for a [SA] for [SD] after you’d already realised it was a garden ornament. Apologise.
You told [SN] they had [SD] to prepare their entrance as [SR], then called them up immediately. Apologise.
You moved the [SC] sign outside [SL] and accidentally redirected everyone arriving for [SE]. Apologise.
You promised [SN] a sample of [SF] at [ST]. You ate it while you were waiting. Apologise.
You signed [SN]’s name on a label for [SB] at [SE] because you assumed it was theirs. Apologise.
You cleared [SO] away from [SL] [SD] before someone needed it again. Apologise.
You told [SN] they’d won [SE] before checking the results. The announcement went out at [ST]. Apologise.
You put a [SC] lid over [SF] and told [SN] it was theirs. It was set aside for a different guest. Apologise.
You made an entrance as [SR] carrying [SO]. Everyone at [SE] had been waiting for a quiet introduction. Apologise.
You asked [SN] for a second look at a [SA] in the middle of [SE]. They lost their train of thought. Apologise.
You left [SB] at [SL] for [SD], then asked someone else to admit they had forgotten it. Apologise.
You saved a draft titled “[SH]” at [ST] and accidentally sent it to the whole group for [SE]. Apologise.
You left the first portion of [SF] for [SN], then served it to someone else at [SL]. Apologise.
You pointed to a [SC] sticker and told [SN] they’d found [SO]. It was on the wrong object. Apologise.
You practised your lines as [SR] while [SN] was trying to work for [SD]. Apologise.
You told [SN] a [SA] was the reason [SO] was missing. You found it in your own things. Apologise.
You opened the doors at [SL] at [ST] before [SN] had finished setting up. Apologise.
You packed [SF] into [SB] and brought it to [SE] without checking who it was for. Apologise.
You put “[SH]” at the top of an invitation to [SE] and signed it with [SN]’s name. Apologise.
You made a [SC] sign for [SL] but hung it somewhere nobody could see for [SD]. Apologise.
You handed [SO] to the person dressed as [SR] and left [SN] waiting for it. Apologise.
You told [SN] that a [SA] had appeared at [SL]. Everyone looked up just as the photo was taken. Apologise.
You started clearing [SF] away from [SE] at [ST] while people were still eating. Apologise.
You said [SB] would keep [SO] safe at [SL], then sent the bag away with the wrong group. Apologise.
You booked a rehearsal as [SR] at [ST] and put it in the calendar for [SE] by mistake. Apologise.
You sent [SN] a [SC] card saying “[SH]” and forgot to include the actual message. Apologise.
You stayed near [SL] to watch a [SA] for [SD] while everyone else carried the supplies. Apologise.
You mailed the [SC] table plan to [SN] after [SE] was over. Apologise for leaving them to improvise.
